writeup.headline: Diamondback rates Hold: strong revenue growth and firm trend offset by a high EV/EBIT valuation.
writeup.thesis: Diamondback scores 60, a Hold, 5 points short of Buy and 16 points above Sell. Growth is the strongest factor at 93, with latest-quarter revenue growth of 51.2% year on year, TTM revenue growth of 21.4%, and growth sped up by 46.5 pp from the previous quarter. Trend scores 69, with the price 9.1% above its 200-day average and only 3.5% below its 52-week high, though shares are 7.5 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days. Valuation drags at 25: EV/EBIT of 64.6x is high in absolute terms and more expensive than at 56 of the last 61 month-ends, while P/S of 3.4x sits near the middle of the last 61 month-ends (cheaper than at 24, more expensive than at 37). News risk is roughly neutral at 54, helped slightly by price-target raises and a new Outperform initiation.
key_risks: EV/EBIT of 64.6x is high in absolute terms and expensive against its own history, leaving little room for disappointment.
Operating margin of 6.3% is thin, and cash to debt of 0.04 points to a debt-heavy balance sheet.
Q3 results due Nov 2 come after an 8-K pre-announcing derivative losses, a mixed signal.
Revenue depends on oil and gas prices; the recent growth spike may not persist.
Shares have lagged SPY and QQQ over the last 126 trading days.
what_would_change: A 5-point score gain would reach Buy, for example if EBIT rises enough to bring EV/EBIT down and lift the valuation score from 25.
Sustained strong growth in the Q3 report plus continued price strength could push the score over 65.
A drop of more than 15 points, such as growth fading sharply alongside a weaker trend or negative news on guidance, would move it to Sell.
